versions.name: Native core
versions.summary: The foundation: native edge rails and the Halo pill on Windows, islands on the wallpaper layer, themes that do not depend on Windows, user-defined contexts.

versions.name: Inbox
versions.summary: Real files for the first time: Desktop and Downloads watching, bins, a Tidy preview, auto-sort for sure things, and one shared undo for every move.

versions.name: Command bar
versions.summary: Alt+Space search and a small command grammar, a configurable hotkey, the Shelf for holding files, and Peek for quick previews.

versions.name: Smart
versions.summary: The local, no-AI helpers: desk health, smart rename, rule suggestions from your own moves, project folders, near-duplicate images, installer clean-up. Plus a guided first run, a per-user installer and signed auto-update.

versions.name: Quick fixes
versions.summary: A round of fixes from daily use: clearer settings, calmer defaults and a steadier Halo.

versions.name: Docks & Halo
versions.summary: Where the Halo and the docks live, and how they get out of your way: over apps, hidden until hover, or on the desktop, with compact modes and drop targets.

versions.name: Panels
versions.summary: Panels that work harder: a fixed action bar, right-click menus everywhere, and panels you add yourself.

versions.name: Shell
versions.summary: A Shell panel for the commands you keep retyping, with a terminal built in later.

versions.name: Projects
versions.summary: What a project should mean in noDesk is still open. The idea on the table is a workspace that lays out its folder, apps, shell presets and notes.

versions.name: Desktop cleanup
versions.summary: An opt-in, reversible cleanup of the Windows desktop: shortcuts sorted into launcher categories, loose files into folders, native icons hidden only while you want them hidden.

versions.name: Follow-ups
versions.summary: What the desktop cleanup left open: checks on a real desktop, shortcuts that show up later, and undo that works from anywhere.

versions.name: Beta
versions.summary: Wider testing once the shape settles: polish, accessibility pass, code signing.

items.title: A real cog for settings
items.summary: The settings icon was a sun. It is a proper cog now.

items.title: A Halo mark that stays put
items.summary: The n no longer slides when the pill grows on hover. A click on the resting pill opens the command bar.

items.title: Home, Art, Dev and Focus contexts
items.summary: A friendlier default set, each with its own layout and accent. Home is the one that stays. Your own contexts are untouched.

items.title: Settings in sections, plus an App section
items.summary: One section open at a time, remembered. The App section adds start with Windows, settings presets you can save, load, export and import, and a Quit button.

items.title: Denser panels and a Panel opacity setting
items.summary: Panels are less see-through by default, and a slider lets you choose how much.

items.title: Upright labels on vertical docks
items.summary: Letters stack top to bottom instead of lying sideways. Rotated text stays available as an option.

items.title: Choose where the Halo and docks sit
items.summary: Over your apps, hidden until you hover, or on the desktop behind them. The Halo defaults to over apps, compact.

items.title: Compact docks with staged reveal
items.summary: A thin strip in the stack's accent colour widens when you point at it and opens the panel after a short dwell you can tune.

items.title: Fix panels that are cut off on one side
items.summary: Open dock panels had a squared-off edge against the screen. They now float just off the edge with rounded corners all round.

items.title: Resize panels
items.summary: Drag an edge or corner. Sizes are remembered per context, and a resize is undoable like any other change.

items.title: Clear drop targets, and drop on the Halo
items.summary: Bins light up while you drag a file to them. Dropping files on the Halo offers actions that fit what you dropped, such as moving them to a bin or holding them on the Shelf, and a move can be undone.

items.title: Frosted-glass blur where Windows allows
items.summary: Tried on Windows 10: the blur cannot be kept inside a panel's shape there, so panels keep the dense see-through look. Windows 11 is worth another try later.

items.title: A drag grid on the desktop
items.summary: A faint dot grid appears while you drag a panel or icon, so things line up. Static when reduced motion is on.

items.title: Progress for slow jobs
items.summary: A line on the Halo and a bar in the panel for scans and other long jobs, with Cancel where it is possible.

items.title: A new logo, app icon and tray icon
items.summary: The Squared nD mark replaces the placeholder: a real multi-size app icon, a mark on the Halo that takes the context accent, and a tray icon with Quit.

items.title: A fixed action bar in each panel
items.summary: The actions for your selection stay in view instead of scrolling away, with one suggestion that fits the moment.

items.title: Right-click menus
items.summary: Open, open with, show in Explorer, copy path, rename, move to a bin, add to the Shelf. Also on noDesk's own surfaces for quick settings, layout and Quit.

items.title: Add your own panels
items.summary: Launcher groups, live folder views, saved searches and notes, each stackable, dockable or floating like any other panel.

items.title: Choose your own scan folders
items.summary: Add folders for noDesk to watch, each set to refresh automatically or only when you ask. Applies without a restart.

items.title: A Shell panel
items.summary: Saved commands with a working folder, opened in Windows Terminal. A command builder fills in values you type each time, suggests commands from your project files and shows exactly what will run.

items.title: A built-in terminal
items.summary: Presets and shells run inside the Shell panel: live output in a real terminal, the processes it started, Stop and Run again, and a watch that tells you when a tool finishes, goes quiet waiting for you, or prints a word you pick.

items.title: Projects, once we decide what they are
items.summary: Postponed for now. Options: a workspace that lays out your folder, apps and notes; plain project folders as today; or leave it to folder panels and launcher groups.

items.title: Hiding the desktop icons safely
items.summary: A spike showed the native icon layer can be hidden and always comes back: after a crash, an Explorer restart or quitting, with every icon position unchanged.

items.title: Sorting desktop shortcuts by what they are
items.summary: Offline, explained and unit-tested: each shortcut gets a category (Code, Games, Office, Web, System and more) with a reason in words; files are grouped by kind.

items.title: A preview before the desktop is cleaned up
items.summary: A sheet shows the suggested categories before anything happens: drag or key shortcuts between them, add, rename or delete a category. Apply makes one Desktop launcher with a tab per category and one Ctrl+Z step; no shortcut file is moved.

items.title: The Desktop launcher, styled for many tabs
items.summary: The launcher made by cleanup is tuned for a dozen categories: roomier tabs, a launch that is quick and clear.

items.title: Hide the native icons while cleanup is on
items.summary: Optional and always reversible: turning it off, quitting or a crash brings every icon back where it was.

items.title: Loose desktop files through Tidy
items.summary: Files on the Desktop use the same preview and plan as Tidy, into folders you can undo.

items.title: Checked by hand on a real desktop
items.summary: Dragging shortcuts between categories, launching from the Desktop launcher, high-DPI screens, the day theme, and an Explorer restart while the icons are hidden.

items.title: New shortcuts offered after a cleanup
items.summary: A shortcut that lands on the Desktop later is suggested for its category instead of waiting for the next full cleanup.

items.title: Undo cleanup from any context
items.summary: Ctrl+Z after a cleanup removes the Desktop launcher everywhere, not only in the context where it was applied.

items.title: An accessibility pass
items.summary: Screen-reader names, keyboard reach and contrast checked on every panel, rail and sheet.

items.title: A signed installer you can download
items.summary: Code signing so Windows does not warn, and a download on this page once the beta opens.
